The Vatican. The world's smallest independent nation-state, a sovereign city nestled within Rome that serves as the spiritual and administrative center of the Roman Catholic Church. Established in its modern political form in nineteen twenty-nine, it claims continuity from Saint Peter's burial site and the papacy's ancient seat. The Vatican is a unique entity—a religious institution with territorial sovereignty, diplomatic recognition, and profound influence on over a billion Catholics worldwide.

The Vatican covers approximately one hundred ten acres on the western bank of the Tiber River within Rome. The Pope is both its absolute monarch and the head of the worldwide Roman Catholic Church, making it a theocracy. It is built upon the traditional burial site of Saint Peter, the apostle whom Jesus declared the "rock" upon which the Church would be built. Saint Peter's Basilica is one of Christianity's holiest sites and a masterpiece of Renaissance architecture, begun in fifteen oh-six and completed in sixteen twenty-six.

Michelangelo designed the basilica's dome and painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, making the Vatican an artistic treasure of immeasurable value. The Papal States ruled vast Italian territories for over a thousand years until Italy's unification in eighteen seventy-one left the Pope trapped within Rome. The Lateran Treaty of nineteen twenty-nine restored papal independence, creating Vatican City as a sovereign microstate with observer status at the United Nations. The Vatican houses one of the world's greatest libraries and the Secret Archives, repositories of centuries of Church documents and diplomatic correspondence that form an incomparable historical record.
